findings.description: The assertion required by the spec sits on the WRITE side and is structurally unreachable; the READ-BACK path performs no duplicate detection at all. Spec text: 'key mark read-back by row identity (symbol), asserting one row per symbol and erroring loudly if violated.' Code: the only one-row-per-symbol check is in render_positions (lib.rs:540-545), a BTreeSet<&Symbol> over snapshot.positions — which is itself a Map<Symbol,_>, so the Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow) branch is unique-by-construction. The code comment (lib.rs:534-539) and both tests (mapping.rs:66-69, 94-102) explicitly concede the branch is 'structurally UNREACHABLE through the real API' and is a 'DEFENSIVE assertion'. The actual read-back, read_marks (lib.rs:817-887), consumes PricePass = BTreeMap<Symbol, PriceReading> (lib.rs:299) — duplicates are collapsed by the container type before sheets-view ever sees them, so a real violation (a human-inserted second row for one symbol on the Positions tab) is silently absorbed by whatever runtime's read_price_pass does, never surfaced, never errored. All three A-runs implement exactly the missing thing: an assertion over an ordered sequence of read-back rows (Vec<MarkRow>/IntoIterator with a row index carried for diagnostics) that returns Err(DuplicateSymbol{symbol, first, dup}) on the second occurrence. All three B-runs independently reconstruct the code's stance as 'defensive assertion, unreachable branch, holds by construction' (B1-004, B2-005, B3-002), which is the inverse of what the spec asks for. Net: the requirement's operative clause ('erroring loudly if violated') is satisfied only by a dead branch on the wrong side of the write/read boundary.

Silent last-write-wins across settle polls — the exact multiplicity behavior the spec's 'error loudly' clause forbids on the other side. read_marks (lib.rs:829-833) does `latest.insert(s.clone(), r.clone())` on every poll, so a second reading for the same symbol overwrites the first with no assertion, no comparison, and no diagnostic. All three B-runs pin this as a requirement (B1-007 'latest.insert overwrites', B2-006 'shall overwrite, never accumulate', B3-007 'latest-wins per symbol'). SHEET-MAP-002 never mentions polling, per-poll readings, or any precedence rule; its only stated position on more-than-one-per-symbol is that it is an error.

The read-back is driven entirely by the caller-supplied `symbols` slice, and any symbol present in the sheet read but absent from that slice is silently discarded. read_marks iterates `for s in symbols { if let Some(r) = pass.get(s) … }` (lib.rs:829-833) and again at lib.rs:848 — the PricePass is never scanned for unexpected entries. An extra/orphan row on the Positions tab therefore produces neither a mark, a degrade, nor an error. Unanimous in B (B1-007 'symbols present in the read pass but not in `symbols` SHALL be ignored', B2-006, B3-006). The spec's 'asserting one row per symbol' says nothing about row-set coverage in either direction, and the code pins the permissive half without stating it.

Absent ≡ Transient is a code-only equivalence with real settle consequences. lib.rs:838 treats `None` alongside Some(Transient) as not-settled (so a never-appearing symbol burns the whole retry window), and lib.rs:873-879 routes `Some(Transient) | None` to the same arm: carry the prior Mark if one exists, else degrade TimedOut. All three B-runs state it as a requirement (B1-008, B2-007, B3-006). Nothing in SHEET-MAP-002 covers a symbol that is missing from the read-back — which is arguably the very 'row identity violated' case the spec means, and it is handled as a benign timeout rather than a loud error.

The 'loud' error's shape and its entire test coverage are pinned by code, not spec. ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow carries only the Symbol (lib.rs:412) and Display is implemented as `write!(f, "{self:?}")` (lib.rs:415-419), producing exactly `DuplicateSymbolRow("AMZN")` — asserted verbatim at mapping.rs:124 on a hand-constructed variant, which is the only test that touches the error at all. All three B-runs elevate the Debug-as-Display detail to a requirement (B1-005, B2-004, B3-003). The spec says only 'erroring loudly', pinning neither the channel (Err vs panic — all three A-runs deliberated this and chose typed Err) nor the payload; all three A-runs carry BOTH offending row numbers so the sheet can actually be repaired, a diagnostic the real error cannot express.

Key-vs-ticker split is code-only and leaves a duplicate the guard cannot catch. The row key and every map key stay the raw ledger Symbol verbatim (lib.rs:577 Cell::Value(symbol.clone()), BTreeMap<Symbol,_> throughout), while the Price (col E) and Quote Date (col M) formulas are built from the alias-resolved ticker via AliasMap::resolve (lib.rs:547, 581, 590), tested at mapping.rs:38-62. B3-005 states the split explicitly ('Symbols SHALL NOT be normalized … an aliased symbol renders =GOOGLEFINANCE("BRK.B","price") while the row key stays BRK'); B1-006 and B2-003 agree. SHEET-MAP-002's parenthetical '(symbol)' never distinguishes ledger symbol from the ticker the read-back cells are actually computed from, so two distinct ledger symbols aliasing to one ticker pass the write-side guard and yield two rows quoting the same instrument — an alias-level duplicate no code path asserts against.

Additional read-back constants and layout pinned by code with no spec counterpart: DATA_START_ROW = 2 with the frozen header at row 1 and each row's anchored formulas computed as `(rows.len() as u32) + DATA_START_ROW` (lib.rs:148, 546, 563-574); Symbol fixed at POSITIONS_HEADER index 0 / column A with Price at E and Quote Date at M (lib.rs:174-188); SettleConfig::default().max_polls = 8 as the bounded retry window (lib.rs:786-790); and the locale-proof quote-date encoding =IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE(t,"tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"") (lib.rs:270-274). B1-002/B2-001/B2-002/B3-004 reconstruct the row-anchoring rule as load-bearing for read-back row identity; B3-007 pins max_polls=8. SHEET-MAP-002 states none of it, so the physical basis of 'row identity' lives only in code.

Open sub-decision, not missing behavior: the spec never defines symbol EQUALITY for the key, and all three A-runs independently invented the same rule — trim + to_ascii_uppercase before comparison, so "aapl " and "AAPL" collide as a duplicate (A1 assumption 2, A2 assumption 4, A3 assumption 4), each justifying it as preventing a silent case-variant split into two marks for one holding. The real code normalizes nothing: keys are the raw Symbol, so BTreeMap equality is byte-exact and case-sensitive (B3-005 confirms this from the code side). Flagged as spec ambiguity rather than spec-traced drift — the normalization has no basis in the EARS text, so it is an A-side assumption artifact; what IS material is that the spec leaves the equality rule wholly open on a requirement whose entire content is a keying rule, and the two directions resolved it oppositely.

notes:
Files read: {scratch}/audit-baseline/crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs and .../tests/mapping.rs.

Why BD-DRIFT rather than B-ONLY: the two directions do not merely each carry surplus — they collide on the same axis. The spec's operative clause is a loud error on duplicate read-back rows; A-side unanimously built that check over an ordered row sequence at the read-back boundary, while B-side unanimously reconstructed the code as placing a self-described unreachable defensive guard on the write side and then silently last-write-wins on the actual read path. Same gap, opposite sides. Finding 1 is that collision; findings 2-4 are the concrete places the read path absorbs violations instead of erroring.

A-side stability (high): all three runs converged on nearly identical shape — a pure `key_marks_by_symbol(rows) -> Result<HashMap<..>, Err>`, trim+ASCII-uppercase normalization, blank/whitespace symbol as an error, fail-fast on the first duplicate, a typed thiserror Err carrying symbol + both offending row numbers, explicit rejection of panic! as inappropriate for a library reading user-editable sheet data, empty input legal, row index as diagnostics-only metadata, no cross-check against the position set. Divergence is cosmetic only (map value = whole MarkRow vs Cents; Vec vs IntoIterator; Cents alias vs newtype).

B-side stability (high): all three pin the same core — symbol in column A / POSITIONS_HEADER[0] as sole read-back key, the render_positions guard as an explicitly *defensive and unreachable* assertion, ViewError Display-as-Debug rendering `DuplicateSymbolRow(\"AMZN\")`, BTreeMap<Symbol,_> at most one entry per symbol for PricePass/marks/degraded, alias-resolved ticker in the formula but raw symbol as key, caller-supplied `symbols` as the drive list with extras ignored, absent-treated-as-Transient, and latest-wins per poll. Variance is only in which secondary constants each run chose to surface (max_polls=8 in B3 only; the verbatim quote-date formula in B2; DATA_START_ROW row arithmetic in all three but at differing precision) — additive, not contradictory.

Assumption artifacts excluded from findings (unanimous A-side, no spec basis): blank/whitespace-only symbol as an error rather than a skipped padded row (A1 asm 3, A2 asm 7, A3 asm 5); fail-fast on the first duplicate rather than accumulating all violations; price parsing being upstream/out of scope; Option<Cents> for an unresolved GOOGLEFINANCE cell. Also noted but not raised: A1/A3 explicitly declined exchange-prefix normalization (NASDAQ:AAPL vs AAPL treated as distinct), which happens to agree with the code's alias handling.

One structural observation worth carrying to the fix: because read_price_pass returns a BTreeMap<Symbol, PriceReading>, sheets-view has no representation in which the violation SHEET-MAP-002 describes can even exist. Any real fix has to change the seam type (an ordered Vec of (row, symbol, reading)) before the loud error the spec demands becomes expressible — the spec cannot be honored by adding a check to read_marks as it stands.
